description_full: Mercari, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the planning, development, and operation of the Mercari marketplace application in Japan and the United States. It operates through Japan Business, US, and Other segments. The company is also involved in the planning, development, and operation of financial services, such as money transfer services, as well as crypto asset and blockchain services. In addition, it engages in the operation of a professional soccer club; and sports facilities, including soccer stadiums. Further, the company engages in the planning and operation of soccer matches, other sports competitions, and various events; and internet service development activities. Mercari, Inc. was incorporated in 2013 and is headquartered in Minato, Japan.

financial_summary: Mercari Inc. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $5.1B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 30% against a 7% cost of capital — a 23-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 70% confirm genuine pricing power.
The company is burning through $92M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 44× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 0.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 31% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
